kf: **Hypertrophic scars** stay within the wound and often settle; **keloids** extend beyond it, persist and recur.
Keloids are much commoner in skin of colour and families; sites: earlobes, jawline, chest, shoulders, upper back.
First line: **silicone gel or sheet** for months; pressure; potent topical steroid under occlusion.
Specialist: intralesional steroid, cryotherapy, laser, excision with adjuvant therapy.
Biopsy an atypical or rapidly growing 'keloid' to exclude DFSP.

sub: Keloids peak at 10–30 years; up to 15–20× more common in people of African descent.

myths: **"Cut it out and it's gone"**: keloids recur in most cases after simple excision.
patho_lead: Raised scars come from **too much collagen** and not enough breakdown.

mech.t: Injury starts normal healing: inflammation, proliferation, remodelling.
TGF-β signalling keeps fibroblasts producing collagen.
Hypertrophic scars stay in the wound; keloids invade surrounding skin with thick, glassy collagen.
mech.cap: Hypertrophic scar (left) within the wound; keloid (right) extends beyond it.

mech.t: Wounds under tension (chest, shoulders) are most prone.

histo: Keloid: thick hyalinised (glassy) collagen bundles; hypertrophic scar: nodules of collagen parallel to the surface.
prog: Hypertrophic scars often improve over 1–2 years; keloids persist.
